title: Published variable value
description:
The value of one variable as it is published by the controller. Used by `shared_variable_update`, `global_variable_update`, `get_variables` and `cleanup_application`.

An int and a float are both published as a plain JSON number, and a float with an integral value is published without a decimal point (`1.0` becomes `1`), so a consumer cannot tell the two apart by looking at the number. A list is always an object with the keys `_ur_list` and `_ur_capacity`. A plain array is a matrix, an array of arrays of numbers. A pose is an object with the key `_ur_pose`. A struct is an object with one key per member. Values that cannot be represented as data (for example a function or a thread) are published as an object with a single `_ur_*` key set to null.

Float.description: Floating point number, published with 8 significant digits. A float with an integral value is published without a decimal point and large magnitudes use exponent notation (`1e+10`), so it can also look like an integer, even one outside the 32 bit range. Not a number and infinity are published as 0.

Matrix.description: A matrix, as rows of numbers. Lists are not published as plain arrays, see `ListWithCapacity`.

Pose.description: Cartesian pose `[x, y, z, rx, ry, rz]`, position in meters and rotation vector in radians.

ListWithCapacity.description: A list together with its capacity.

Placeholder.description: A value that has no data representation, for example a function or a thread. It is published as an object with a single `_ur_*` key set to null.

Struct.description: A struct, one entry per member. Member names starting with `_ur_` are reserved for the other value types.
